summary: PARTIAL is correct. Parts (a) and (b) are in place and both are in the Hub-vendored Ryco 7bc39eec3. #710 (60633eff3) made the inbound path zero-copy: the WS ArrayBuffer is handed over, the hub-session data payload is borrowed, and the engine's owned, payload and delivered copies are gone. ws.send also no longer copies. 2cb0d3f5e replaced the full canonical re-encode and compare with a spliced prefix/head/suffix check (840 to 32 us per 256 KiB on Node) and stopped copying outbound chunks the engine already owns. Part (c) is not done. There is no Worker for HostedHubSession, HostedRelayEngine or the E2EE channel. On browsers, noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 still runs on the main thread, as one synchronous call per reassembled record (about 9 ms for a 3 MB message on desktop V8). Small copy leftovers remain: the facade copy at relaySocket.ts:244, the assembler copy and concat, and the outbound encodeRelayFrame and hub-session header copies.

evidence.note: Inbound ArrayBuffer is wrapped without slice (was data.slice(0)); changed in 60633eff3.
send passes the view straight to ws.send (was Uint8Array.from(bytes).buffer).
decodeHubSessionFrame(bytes, { borrowDataPayload: true }). The codec returns a subarray at packages/shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts:112. Dropped-data paths zero the payload at :333 and :338.

decodeRelayFrame runs on the handed-over buffer, which is zeroed at :772; the owned copy is gone. cborg's decode still copies the payload once (byte-utils slice -> data.slice). That is now the single necessary inbound copy.
frame.payload is queued as is. #drainInbound hands it to the assembler at :1204 without the delivered copy.
Outbound chunk copy now runs only when chunk === payload; the same at :1121 (2cb0d3f5e).
isCanonicalEncoding spliced check for byte-string payloads of 1 KiB or more, called at :181. The cborg decode plus the Schema decode at :275 remain, but there is no full re-encode or compare.

this.#engine.send(Uint8Array.from(b)) remains. Hosted RPC uses RpcSerialization.layerJson (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:517), so writes are strings and b is already a fresh TextEncoder buffer (:235). Every engine sink copies again: e2ee at relayE2eeChannel.ts:789, negotiating at relayEngine.ts:660, legacy unchunked at :593. The facade copy is only ever zeroed on the legacy error path (relayEngine.ts:582), and that path is the only reason the copy exists for caller-owned views.

The assembler still does Uint8Array.from(body) plus a fill per chunk, then a concat at :319. The input is already engine-owned and is mutated by the assembler anyway. The server caller apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:249 also hands its buffer over.
Outbound data frames are still copied to prepend the 5-byte header. encodeRelayFrame (relayCodec.ts:294-308) still does a Schema decode plus a cborg encode that copies the payload.
Native fast paths are never installed in browsers; only installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives (relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts:408) installs them, for server and desktop. Web AEAD is noble (relayE2eeNoise.ts:1).
intercept calls session.unprotect(payload) synchronously on the whole reassembled record. A multi-MB message is one long main-thread task.

HostedHubSession, the engine (runtime.ts:89) and the E2EE provider are all built on the main thread. The only web Workers are the diff and PWA ones (apps/web/src/lib/diffParseOffThread.ts:152, diffWorkerPool.ts:3, pwa/lifecycle.ts). Nothing relay-related appeared in f1be4abc7..HEAD. The Hub CSP already allows worker-src 'self' blob: (ryco-hub origin/main src/http/securityHeaders.ts:35).

remaining: (c) is untouched. The receive path (WS message -> HostedHubSession.#receive -> HostedRelayEngine.#receive/decodeRelayFrame -> RelayMessageAssembler -> relayE2eeChannel.intercept/session.unprotect, which is noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 over the whole record -> onData) and the send path (TextEncoder -> facade copy -> channel.submit copy -> noble seal -> prepareRelayMessage -> encodeRelayFrame -> encodeHubSessionFrame -> ws.send) all run on the web main thread. Leftover copies: (1) apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:244 redundantly copies the fresh TextEncoder buffer for every RPC write and leaves that plaintext copy unzeroed; (2) packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts:307/:319 makes a retained copy plus a concat per chunked message; (3) outbound encodeRelayFrame cborg copy and hubSessionCodec.ts:70 header copy. The value of (c) is lower than the report assumed: the web phone tier is frozen behind the get-the-app interstitial (AGENTS.md), so the 50-70 ms phone estimate mostly no longer applies to web. On desktop the cost is about 9 ms per 3 MB message, a single long task during screenshot-sized RPCs.
fixDefects: No defects found in the implemented parts. Zeroization holds: the engine zeroes the borrowed buffer after decode (relayEngine.ts:772), the session zeroes dropped data payloads (hostedHubSession.ts:333, :338), and the queue zeroes sent chunks after the synchronous browser ws.send copy. The 5-byte hub-session header in front of the borrowed view is not zeroed, but it only holds the kind and stream id. A data frame for a stream with zero message listeners would skip zeroing, and with several listeners the second would see zeros (hostedHubSession.ts:342). Neither is reachable, because exactly one engine listener is registered per logical stream. Sibling, not part of this web finding: apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:309 still copies inbound with data.slice(0). Its send copy at :383 is deliberate, since React Native may send asynchronously.
implementationSketch: Small leftovers (S, low risk, no decision needed): (1) In BrowserHostedRelaySocket.send (apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:232-247), when typeof data === 'string', call this.#engine.send(encoded) on the TextEncoder buffer with no copy, then encoded.fill(0) in a finally. This is safe because every engine sink has already copied synchronously by then (relayE2eeChannel.ts:789, relayEngine.ts:660, :593, and splitRelayMessage), and it improves zeroization. Keep the copy for caller-owned ArrayBuffer/view inputs. Alternatively, drop it entirely and remove the caller-buffer fill at relayEngine.ts:582 so the engine never mutates caller memory. Tests in apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.test.ts: the engine receives the encoded buffer, it is zeroed after send, a caller Uint8Array is never mutated (including the legacy oversize refusal), and DOMException mapping is unchanged. (2) In RelayMessageAssembler.push (packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts:305-309), retain the body subarray instead of Uint8Array.from(body) plus fill. The concat loop at :321-325 and reset at :334 already zero the parts. Document that push takes ownership; both callers (relayEngine.ts:1204, apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:249) already hand over. Extend relayMessageChunks.test.ts so the inputs are zeroed after completion and reset. (3) Optional: let encodeHubSessionFrame accept a pre-reserved 5-byte header slot, or have the engine encode the relay frame into a buffer with header headroom, to drop the hub-session copy. Part (c) (L): add a module worker apps/web/src/hostedHub/relayDataPlane.worker.ts (worker.format 'es'). It owns the physical hub-session WebSocket, HostedHubSession, one HostedRelayEngine per logical channel, and the E2EE provider, and posts only decrypted RPC messages as transferable ArrayBuffers, plus status, invalidation and failure events. The main thread keeps hostedHubController and hostedHubStore and a thin proxy that implements the current HostedHubSession surface (resume, probe, createSocket) and the BrowserHostedRelaySocket EventTarget facade. Lifecycle decisions (expireSession, failure, generation checks) stay on the main thread. The worker caches nothing and is terminated on sign-out or disposal. The ticket and DPoP CryptoKeys cross by structured clone. The E2EE verification display, the §12.1 latch and E2eeNxHandshake UI state must be bridged over messages. A cheaper interim, if (c) is too large: an async AEAD seam used only for records of at least about 64 KiB, running noble chacha20poly1305 in a small crypto worker. intercept and protectRecord are already async and serialized, but session.unprotect/protect would have to become async, and session keys would cross threads. Validate with the full web browser suite (apps/web test:browser, including E2eeNxHandshake.browser.tsx and the maliciousRelay tests rerun against the worker), the hosted reconnect and stale-generation tests, and a long-task PerformanceObserver harness that streams a 3 MB RPC.
decisionReason: Part (c) moves the account Hub-session socket (which owns its own reconnect, backoff and probe) and the E2EE channel with its session keys into a Worker. That touches the AGENTS.md rule that hosted lifecycle recovery has a single owner, moves key material across threads, and changes where the E2EE verification and latch state lives, so it needs owner and security sign-off. The interim crypto-worker option also moves session keys across threads and makes the record-layer API async. The small copy leftovers (relaySocket.ts:244 string branch, assembler copy) need no decision.
correction: Line nits only: the TextEncoder branch is at relaySocket.ts:235 (not :234), and engine #receive is at :760 with the decode at :768. One nuance: the facade copy at relaySocket.ts:244 is not purely redundant for caller-owned views, because it shields the caller's buffer from the legacy error-path zeroing at relayEngine.ts:582. It is purely redundant for the string branch, which is the only branch hosted RPC uses (layerJson). Implemented (b) also differs from the proposal: the cborg decode and Schema decode still run, and only the re-encode and compare were reduced to the envelope. The measured cost of 32 us per 256 KiB makes that adequate. The web phone tier is now frozen, which lowers the value of (c) further.
